correctness.rationale: For every k≥1, a single exact three-branch update identity follows from degree 2k−1 strict neighbor vote, and classifies every orbit by total ones and conformist ones. Counting all off-central and central states gives four+B_k immediately periodic, 4^k−C_k−2 entering at time one, and C_k−2−B_k at time two. Central balanced conformist count yields B_k two-periodic states; all others enter one four-cycle. Direct vertexwise enumeration for k=1,...,8 independently matched every formula. Stirling proves the asymptotic for even k. No infinite conclusion relies on finite tests.

value.rationale: The complete balanced majority/minority clique is a canonical population model, and the quantified questions are its natural microscopic attractor basin sizes and relaxation shells, not arbitrary numerical slices. The result distinguishes a unique globally attracting four-cycle for odd k from central-binomial many isolated two-cycle orbits for even k, with a sharp finite-population and critical-window random-initialization law. These are structurally meaningful properties not supplied by general primitive-period existence statements.
